items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, natural emphasis on numbers, a short comic pause before each punchline (especially 'Snow doesn't stand a chance', 'NASA thought so' and the last line before the sign-off). Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish.
lines: You could stand here, in Antarctica, and see no ice at all.
The story goes, it hasn't rained here in two million years.
So how? This valley sits beside the biggest ice sheet on Earth.
First, the mountains. They wall off the glaciers trying to flow in.
Then the wind finishes the job.
Freezing air pours off the ice sheet, warms as it drops, and scours the valleys, with gusts measured near one hundred and forty kilometres an hour.
Some snow does fall, about ten centimetres a year.
But this air is so dry, the snow turns straight into vapour. In summer, it can vanish in hours.
So nothing here gets wet. Nothing rots either.
Seals that wandered inland lie freeze-dried, some maybe two thousand years old.
Cold, dry, dead-looking... sound familiar? NASA thought so.
Scientists have tested Mars ideas here since the Viking missions of the nineteen seventies.
Because the closest thing to Mars isn't in space. It's at the bottom of our own planet.
Here's the twist. Life still made it here, hiding inside the rocks.
No rain. No rent. Great view.
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
